raw_html:
1.Calculating a Double Integral Using Lower and Upper Riemann Sums?

Let R=[−5,−2]×[−6,−1] be a region in the xy-plane, and let P be a partition of R, where

P1={x0,x1,…,xm},P2={y0,y1,…,yn},P=P1×P2.

Calculate the double integral

∬Rf(x,y)dA,

where f is a function such that mij=Mij=3 for all partitions P of R, and mij and Mij are the minimum and maximum values of f respectively in each subregion Rij.

kp_title: Calculating a Double Integral Using the Mean Value of X and Y
raw_html:
4.Calculating a Double Integral Using the Mean Value of X and Y?

Let R=[5,6]×[1,3] be a region in the xy-plane, and let f(x,y) be a function defined over R. The lower and upper Riemann sums corresponding to an arbitrary partition P of R are given by L(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1n(2xi−1−3yj)ΔxiΔyj,U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1n(2xi−3yj−1)ΔxiΔyj.

Using the definition of the double integral in terms of L(f,P) and U(f,P), compute ∬Rf(x,y)dA.

Hint: You may wish to make use of the following result: ∑i=1m∑j=1n(xi−1+xi)ΔxiΔyj=(xm2−x02)(yn−y0)

5.Calculating a Double Integral Using the Mean Value of X and Y?

Let R=[1,3]×[8,10] be a region in the xy-plane, and let f(x,y) be a function defined over R. The lower and upper Riemann sums corresponding to an arbitrary partition P of R are given by L(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1n(2yj−1−4xi−3)ΔxiΔyj,U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1n(2yj−4xi−1−3)ΔxiΔyj.

Using the definition of the double integral in terms of L(f,P) and U(f,P), compute ∬Rf(x,y)dA.

Hint: You may wish to make use of the following results: ∑i=1m∑j=1n(xi−1+xi)ΔxiΔyj=(xm2−x02)(yn−y0)∑i=1m∑j=1nΔxiΔyj=(xm−x0)(yn−y0)
